links.outcome: Self-reported nursing informatics competency and ethical awareness of AI use
links.effect: The six-week generative AI education program improved nursing informatics competency more than control (p < 0.01), sustained at 4 weeks. Ethical awareness of AI use, self-efficacy, and EBP also improved (all p < 0.01), but these were unadjusted for multiplicity.
links.quote: Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated a significantly greater improvement in nursing informatics competency, the pre-specified primary outcome (p < 0.01), sustained at the four-week follow-up.

links.outcome: Self-reported nursing informatics competency following generative AI education
links.effect: The intervention improved self-reported nursing informatics competency versus control (p < 0.01), sustained at the four-week follow-up.
links.quote: Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated a significantly greater improvement in nursing informatics competency, the pre-specified primary outcome (p < 0.01), sustained at the four-week follow-up.

links.effect: The intervention group demonstrated greater improvements for ethical awareness of AI use (p < 0.01).
links.quote: Greater improvements were also observed for the secondary outcomes-general self-efficacy, ethical awareness of AI use, and evidence-based practice (all p < 0.01)-though these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating given the absence of multiplicity adjustment.
